item.title: obsidian-local-rest-api
item.description:
Source: https://github.com/coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api
Full OpenAPI Spec: obsidian-local-rest-api-openapi.yaml All endpoints (except GET /) require Bearer token authentication:Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key> Find the API key in Obsidian Settings > Plugins > Local REST API. HTTPS: https://127.0.0.1:27124 (self-signed cert) HTTP: http://127.0.0.1:27123 The plugin generates a self-signed certificate on first run. The cert can be fetched from /obsidian-local-rest-api.crt.GET / response:{ "authenticated": true, "ok": "OK", "service": "Obsidian Local REST API", "versions": { "obsidian": "...", "self": "..." } } GET (read file): Default Accept: returns raw markdown (text/markdown) Accept: application/vnd.olrapi.note+json: returns JSON with parsed frontmatter, tags, stats Accept: application/vnd.olrapi.document-map+json: returns headings, block refs, frontmatter fields NoteJson schema:{ "content": "string (markdown)", "frontmatter": {}, "path": "string", "stat": { "ctime": 0, "mtime": 0, "size": 0 }, "tags": ["string"] } GET (directory listing): Returns {"files": [{"path": "…", "stat": {…}}]} PUT (create/overwrite): Body: file content Content-Type: text/markdown for notes If-None-Match: * header: only create if file doesn't exist (returns 412 if it does) POST (append): Body: content to append Content-Type: text/markdown Content is appended to end of file DELETE: Returns 204 on success, 404 if not found The PATCH method enables targeted content modifications within a note.Required Headers:Optional Headers:Examples:Append under a heading:PATCH /vault/path/to/note.md Operation: append Target-Type: heading Target: Heading 1::Subheading 1:1:1 Content-Type: text/markdown Hello Replace a frontmatter field:PATCH /vault/path/to/note.md Operation: replace Target-Type: frontmatter Target: status Content-Type: application/json "done" Append to block reference:PATCH /vault/path/to/note.md Operation: append Target-Type: block Target: 2d9b4a Content-Type: text/markdown New content here Same methods as vault files (GET, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) but operates on the currently open file in Obsidian. No {filename} parameter needed.{period} values: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearlySame request/response semantics as vault file operations.Simple Search:POST /search/simple/?query=search+terms Returns matching filenames with context snippets.Response:[ { "filename": "path/to/note.md", "score": 0.95, "matches": [{ "match": { "start": 0, "end": 10 }, "context": "..." }] } ] Structured Search:POST /search/ Content-Type: application/vnd.olrapi.dataview.dql+txt TABLE file.name, file.mtime FROM "folder" WHERE contains(tags, "#coffee") Or with JsonLogic:POST /search/ Content-Type: application/vnd.olrapi.jsonlogic+json {"and": [{"glob": [{"var": "path"}, "daily/*"]}]} GET /commands/ response:{ "commands": [ { "id": "global-search:open", "name": "Search: Search in all files" }, { "id": "graph:open", "name": "Graph view: Open graph view" } ] } POST /open/{filename}?newLeaf=true Opens the specified file in Obsidian's interface. Creates the file if it doesn't exist.All errors return:{ "errorCode": 40149, "message": "A brief description of the error." } Error codes are 5-digit numbers unique to each error type.
Based on the project spec, these are the most relevant endpoints: GET / - Check if API is available (connectivity test) PUT /vault/{filename} - Create new notes (coffee logs, music sets) PATCH /vault/{filename} - Append under headers (journal entries) GET /vault/{dirpath}/ - List files in directory (populate dynamic dropdowns) POST /search/ - Dataview queries for dynamic selects by tag

item.title: CONCEPTS
item.description:
Atomic concept notes — durable, reusable knowledge about the patterns, mental models, and primitives that make Pour what it is. ADRs record decisions; concepts record the vocabulary those decisions are stated in.
The-3-Tier-Data-Fallback — How `dynamic_select` populates without perceived latency: transport → cache → empty/freetext. The read side of the dynamic-data pipeline.
Inline-Note-Creation — The write side of the same pipeline: novel values entered into `dynamic_select` fields auto-create stub or template-driven notes in the vault before the parent capture is written.
Some core Pour concepts live in ADRs or specs rather than here. Treat these as the canonical reference for the concept; this index just makes the cross-link explicit.
ADR-001-Hybrid-Transport-Layer — API-first writes with reqwest to the Obsidian Local REST API, falling back to std::fs. The transport layer is the boundary every other subsystem treats as a black box.
ADR-005-PWA-Companion — The phone-pocket companion to the terminal capture surface. Same engine, different shell.
pour-design-spec — Source of truth for the capture loop, dashboard, summary view, append vs. create modes, and field → output mapping.
pour-preset-hierarchy — Hierarchical drilldown picker concept (preset_axes), as distinct from the legacy linear preset cycler.
pour-api-contract — Wire-shape contract that the PWA companion and any future client speaks.
field-types — The vocabulary of capture: text, number, static_select, dynamic_select, textarea, composite_array, plus modifiers like wikilink, allow_create, show_when, preset_exclude, list.
Unresolved wikilinks below are intentional — they mark concepts worth promoting to atomic notes when the next mention lands. Click any of them in Obsidian's graph to scaffold the note.
Capture-Reflex — The ethos: capture must be a reflex, not a workflow. Sub-second latency from intent to written file.
Atomic-Note-Fallback — When the API is down in append mode, Pour writes a timestamped standalone note instead of failing — zero data loss as a non-negotiable.
Sub-Form-Overlay — The modal form that opens inside a parent form for template-driven creation. Preserves keyboard flow; never spawns a separate process or window.
Conditional-Visibility — show_when rules and the `visible_field_indices` discipline that keeps navigation, validation, and output bounded to visible fields.
Idempotency-Key — How the PWA survives offline replay without duplicating captures. See pour-api-contract. CONCEPTS.base in the 00 index/ directory is an Obsidian Bases database definition that provides a table view of all concepts, filtered and grouped by tag. It is not a markdown document — open it via the Obsidian Bases plugin or view below :)All Concepts3 resultsSort0Filter0PropertiesSearchNewShowing 3file name

item.title: Inline-Note-Creation
item.description:
When a dynamic_select field has allow_create = true, Pour extends the capture flow to include vault-side note creation. This closes the loop between data entry and data management — the user never leaves the TUI to scaffold a new option. The user types a value that doesn't match any existing option in the dropdown. The dropdown shows + Create "{value}" as a visual affordance. On form submit, Pour detects the novel value and auto-creates a bare note at {source}/{value}.md with minimal frontmatter (date only). The note is created before the main module output is written, so any wikilink = true references resolve immediately in Obsidian. The local cache is updated so subsequent form loads include the new option without a transport round-trip. This feature extends The-3-Tier-Data-Fallback with an output side. The fallback pipeline handles reading options into the TUI; inline creation handles writing new options back to the vault. Together they form a closed loop:Vault ──[fetch]──> Cache ──> Dropdown ──[novel value]──> Auto-create ──> Vault When all three tiers fail and the dropdown is empty, allow_create fields accept freetext input (Tier 3 behavior). The submitted value triggers note creation, seeding the cache for future sessions.User-typed values are sanitized before becoming filenames: Characters invalid in cross-platform filenames (: ? * < > | " \ /) are replaced with - Consecutive dashes are collapsed Leading/trailing dashes and whitespace are trimmed Windows reserved device names (CON, NUL, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9) are rejected Empty results after sanitization are skipped Duplicate detection is case-insensitive and checks both the raw typed value and its sanitized form against existing options.Note creation is best-effort. If the transport layer fails (network error, permission issue), the main form write still proceeds. The failure is logged to stderr but does not block the user's capture flow.By default, inline creation produces a bare stub — a note with only a date field. For richer notes, add a create_template reference to the field:[[modules.coffee.fields]] name = "bean" field_type = "dynamic_select" prompt = "Bean" source = "Coffee/Beans" allow_create = true wikilink = true create_template = "bean" post_create_command = "templater:run" # optional — fires an Obsidian command after creation When the user types a novel value, a sub-form overlay appears with the template's fields. The user fills them in without leaving Pour, and the created note gets full structured frontmatter.The overlay is a centered modal that appears over the main form: Shows the template's fields (text, number, static_select) Tab/Shift+Tab navigates fields Enter on the submit button creates the note Esc cancels without creating anything Falls back to bare stub creation if the terminal is too small post_create_command fires an Obsidian command via the REST API after note creation. This bridges Pour's data capture with Obsidian plugins: Pour writes frontmatter (structured data it collected) Templater (or any plugin) adds body content, formatting, and dynamic expressions Only fires when connected via API; silently skipped on filesystem transport Templates are defined at the top level of config.toml:[templates.bean] path = "Coffee/Beans/{{name}}.md" [[templates.bean.fields]] name = "roaster" field_type = "text" prompt = "Roaster" [[templates.bean.fields]] name = "origin" field_type = "static_select" prompt = "Origin" options = ["Ethiopia", "Colombia", "Kenya"]
{{name}} is replaced with the user's typed value. The path also supports strftime tokens (%Y, %m, %d). See field-types > Templates for the full schema reference.# Basic — bare stub creation [[modules.coffee.fields]] name = "bean" field_type = "dynamic_select" prompt = "Bean" source = "Coffee/Beans" allow_create = true wikilink = true # Advanced — template-driven creation with Templater hook [[modules.coffee.fields]] name = "bean" field_type = "dynamic_select" prompt = "Bean" source = "Coffee/Beans" allow_create = true wikilink = true create_template = "bean" post_create_command = "templater:run"
See field-types for the full allow_create, wikilink, create_template, and post_create_command reference.

item.title: The-3-Tier-Data-Fallback
item.description:
Used for populating dynamic_select UI fields without perceived latency in the ratatui form flow.When the TUI initializes a form that requires dynamic data, it executes fetch_options() using a strict three-tier degradation path:
Tier 1 (Transport): Attempts to read the live directory via the active transport layer (API or FS). Tier 2 (Cache): If transport fails or is slow, it queries the atomic local JSON cache at ~/.pour/cache/state.json. Tier 3 (Empty Fallback): If cache is empty or corrupt, it returns an empty vector, dynamically shifting the UI to accept free-text input rather than a strict select list.
This fallback behavior is part of the broader System-Architecture-Overview and is called out in sprint-4-data-fetching-report.Note: Results are always normalized to file stems (stripping .md) before being cached.
When allow_create = true on a dynamic_select field, the fallback pipeline gains a write path. Novel values entered via freetext (at any tier) trigger auto-creation of bare notes on form submit, seeding the cache for future sessions. See Inline-Note-Creation for details.

item.title: sprint-5-tui-report
item.description: Implement the terminal UI layer: app state management, three screen views (dashboard, form, summary), event handling, and top-level wiring that dispatches rendering and input to the correct view. App struct: config, transport, screen enum (Dashboard/Form/Summary), selected_module, form_state, summary_state, sorted module_keys FormState: field_values HashMap, field_options HashMap, active_field index, validation_errors, cursor_position SummaryState: message, file_path (Option), transport_mode App::new(config, transport) — starts on Dashboard, sorts module keys alphabetically App::init_form(module_key) — populates defaults and static_select options, returns None for unknown modules App::validate_form(module, form_state) — checks required fields and number parsing, skips empty optional numbers 9 tests in tests/app.rs render(app, frame) — vertical field list with prompt label, current value, required marker, active field highlight Text/number fields: inline input with cursor indicator; textarea: first-line preview with ellipsis; static/dynamic select: scrollable options popup handle_key(app, key) -> FormAction — Tab/Shift-Tab between fields, Enter submit (or confirm select), Esc cancel, Up/Down cycle select options, Char/Backspace/Left/Right for text editing Number fields filter input to digits, decimal, and minus sign Footer shows key hints or validation errors FormAction enum: None, Submit, Cancel render(app, frame) — header with "Pour" title + connection status (API/File System), navigable module list using display_name, footer key hints Zero-module edge case: shows "No modules configured" message handle_key(app, key) -> DashboardAction — Up/Down navigate with wrapping, Enter select module, q quit DashboardAction enum: None, Quit, SelectModule render(app, frame) — success (green header, file path, transport mode) or error (red header, error message) handle_key(key) -> SummaryAction — Enter (dashboard), a (another entry/same module), q (quit) SummaryAction enum: None, Quit, Dashboard, AnotherEntry pub mod dashboard; pub mod form; pub mod summary; Action enum: None, Quit, Submit, Navigate(Screen) render(app, frame) — dispatches to correct view based on app.screen handle_event(app, key) -> Action — dispatches to correct handler, manages screen transitions: Dashboard: SelectModule -> init_form + navigate to Form Form: Cancel -> clear form + navigate to Dashboard; Submit -> bubble up Summary: Dashboard -> clear summary; AnotherEntry -> re-init form for same module src/lib.rs already declared pub mod app; pub mod tui; (from task scaffolding) Fixed pre-existing clippy warnings: collapsible_if in app.rs (2) and form.rs (1) Fixed unused import FormState in tests/app.rs TUI rendering not unit-tested: Ratatui render functions produce terminal output that requires a mock backend to assert on. App state logic (the testable surface) is covered by tests/app.rs. Visual correctness will be validated manually. Select field interaction model: Up/Down cycles options immediately (value updates in real-time), Enter confirms and advances to next field. This avoids a separate "dropdown open" state. Screen transitions managed in wiring layer: Individual view handlers return typed action enums. The wiring layer in tui/mod.rs translates those into screen transitions and state mutations. Views never mutate app.screen directly. Number input filtering: Form handler rejects non-numeric characters at input time (digits, decimal, minus only). Validation still runs on submit to catch malformed values like "3.2.1". src/ lib.rs — pub mod app, config, data, output, transport, tui app.rs — App state, FormState, SummaryState, Screen enum config.rs — Config, VaultConfig, ModuleConfig, FieldConfig, validation data/ mod.rs — fetch_options() with 3-tier fallback cache.rs — Cache with atomic JSON persistence output/ mod.rs — write_create(), write_append() orchestration frontmatter.rs — YAML frontmatter generation template.rs — path + append template rendering transport/ mod.rs — Transport enum with connect() fallback api.rs — Obsidian REST API client fs.rs — Direct filesystem writer tui/ mod.rs — render() + handle_event() dispatch, Action enum dashboard.rs — Module list with connection status form.rs — Field input with select popups summary.rs — Write result display main.rs — Entry point (placeholder) main.rs: Wire up the actual TUI event loop (terminal init, render loop, event polling, write orchestration on Submit) Dynamic select data loading: Connect data::fetch_options() to form init for dynamic_select fields Error handling in main: Graceful config load errors, transport connect failures Manual testing: End-to-end with a real Obsidian vault

item.title: sprint-6-integration-report
item.description: Wire all subsystems together into a working binary so that cargo run launches a TUI dashboard and cargo run -- <module> opens a form for direct entry. This is the final sprint of v1. #[tokio::main] async entry point CLI arg parsing: no args = dashboard, one arg = fast-path direct to form Config load via Config::load() with user-friendly stderr error + exit(1) on failure Transport connect via Transport::connect(&config).await (auto-fallback from API to filesystem) App::new(config, transport) builds central state Fast path: validates module name exists, sets selected_module index, calls init_form(), fetches dynamic_select options Unknown module name prints available modules to stderr and exits with code 1 Panic hook: std::panic::set_hook restores terminal before printing panic info Terminal lifecycle: ratatui::init() / ratatui::restore() with clean teardown on all exit paths Main loop in run_loop(): terminal.draw(|frame| tui::render(&app, frame)) event::poll(100ms) + event::read() for crossterm events Ctrl+C always breaks cleanly Routes key events through tui::handle_event(&mut app, key_event) Action::Quit breaks the loop Action::Navigate(Screen::Form) triggers dynamic option fetch for new form Action::Submit calls handle_submit() for validation + write + summary transition Action::None continues fetch_dynamic_options() scans module fields for FieldType::DynamicSelect, collects (field_name, source) pairs Calls data::fetch_options(&transport, &source, &mut cache) for each, populating form_state.field_options Invoked on fast-path init AND on dashboard module selection (Navigate to Form) Cache loaded once at startup via Cache::load(), persisted after each write via cache.save() (best-effort, ignores save errors) Config load failure: stderr message + exit code 1 (no TUI initialized) Unknown module fast-path: stderr with available module list + exit code 1 Transport connect: already fallback-safe (API -> filesystem) Write failure on submit: SummaryState populated with error message, file_path = None, displayed as "Error" header in red on summary screen Validation failure on submit: errors stored in form_state.validation_errors, displayed inline in form footer, form stays open (no screen transition) Panic: hook restores terminal before printing panic, so the user sees the panic message in a clean terminal Main loop IO error: terminal restored, error printed to stderr, exit code 1 The main loop is intentionally synchronous within each iteration: draw, poll, handle, act. The fetch_dynamic_options and handle_submit calls are awaited inline, which means the UI blocks during transport operations. This is acceptable for v1 because: Filesystem writes are near-instant API calls have a 5-second timeout True background async would require channels or tokio::spawn + shared state, adding complexity disproportionate to the UX gain main.rs owns: CLI parsing, config load, terminal lifecycle, event loop, submit orchestration, cache persistence tui/mod.rs owns: event routing to screen handlers, action dispatch app.rs owns: form initialization, validation output/ owns: write execution (frontmatter, template, transport calls) data/ owns: option fetching with 3-tier fallback, cache storage Background async refresh of dynamic selects (options load before first render, but don't refresh in background) Multiple-argument CLI support (only one module at a time) Logging/tracing (structured logging is a future sprint) Undo/confirmation before write src/main.rs — complete rewrite from placeholder to full integration The main event loop and submit handler are inherently difficult to unit test (they own terminal state and async I/O). All component logic they call into (config, app, transport, output, data) has thorough test coverage. Manual verification: cargo run launches dashboard, cargo run -- <module> opens form directly.

item.title: sprint-4-data-fetching-report
item.description: Implement the cache layer and dynamic data fetching with 3-tier fallback (transport -> cache -> empty) for populating dynamic select dropdowns. Cache struct backed by ~/.cache/pour/state.json load() / load_from() — returns empty cache on missing or corrupt file (no panics) get(source) — returns Option<Vec<String>> for a source path set(source, items) — updates entry with UTC timestamp via chrono save() — atomic persist to disk (temp file + rename), creates parent directories Uses serde_json for serialization, dirs::cache_dir() for platform path 6 tests: round-trip, missing file, corrupt file, parent dir creation, unknown source, overwrite fetch_options(transport, source_path, cache) -> Vec<String> — async 3-tier fallback Tier 1: transport.list_directory() (API with FS fallback handled by transport layer) Tier 2: cache.get() for previously fetched items Tier 3: empty vec (TUI will offer freetext input) Results normalized to file stems before caching (strips .md extension, filters directory entries) On successful transport fetch, updates cache in-memory (caller saves) 5 tests: transport success + cache population, normalization, transport fail -> cache fallback, both miss -> empty, empty dir -> cache fallback Transport::append_under_heading() now delegates to heading-aware FsWriter::append_under_heading() instead of plain append_to_file() Updated dispatcher test to use a file with actual heading content CRITICAL — API vs FS return shape mismatch: fetch_options cached raw transport results without normalizing. API returns "Ethiopia.md", FS returns "Ethiopia". Fixed: added normalize_items() that strips .md extensions and filters directory entries before caching. MAJOR — Non-atomic cache save: Cache::save() wrote directly, risking corruption on crash. Fixed: now uses temp file + rename (same pattern as FsWriter). MAJOR — No path traversal validation: Config source field accepted ../../etc/secrets. Fixed: Config::validate() now rejects source paths containing ... Added test. Minor — default_cache_path() relative fallback: Falls back to .cache if dirs::cache_dir() returns None. Accepted for v1 (exotic platform edge case). Minor — ApiClient::new uses .expect(): Pre-existing from Sprint 2. Deferred — reqwest::Client::builder().build() effectively never fails. All foundation layers are complete: Config (Sprint 1) — types, loading, validation (incl. path traversal check) Transport (Sprint 2) — API client, FS writer, heading-aware dispatcher with fallback Output (Sprint 3) — frontmatter generation, template rendering, write orchestration Data (Sprint 4) — cache layer, normalized dynamic fetch with 3-tier fallback Sprint 5 (TUI) can begin: app state, dashboard, form, and summary views.

item.title: sprint-3-output-pipeline-report
item.description:
Sprint 3 implemented the output rendering pipeline: YAML frontmatter generation, template rendering for paths and append content, and write orchestration that routes field values through the correct pipeline based on module write mode. All three tasks passed inspection with cargo check, cargo test (59 tests), cargo clippy, and cargo fmt -- --check all clean.generate_frontmatter(fields: &[(String, String)]) -> String with: Hand-built YAML output (no serde_yaml dependency for writing) ---
key: value
---
 block format Auto-injects date field (today via chrono::Local) if not already present, always first Explicit date values are preserved and placed first Empty values are silently skipped Values containing YAML-special characters (:, #, {, }, [, ], etc.) are double-quoted with escaped internal quotes Leading - triggers quoting (YAML list indicator) but - mid-value does not (avoids quoting dates like 2025-01-15) Comma-separated values (detected by ", " delimiter) are emitted as YAML lists with - item syntax 7 tests: auto-date injection, explicit date preservation/ordering, empty value skipping, special character quoting, comma-to-list conversion, list items with special chars, all-empty-fields edge case.Two functions: render_path(template: &str) -> String -- chrono strftime substitution via Local::now().format(). Converts "Journal/%Y/%Y-%m-%d.md" to "Journal/2026/2026-03-30.md". render_append_template(template: &str, fields: &HashMap<String, String>) -> String -- {{field}} placeholder substitution with special {{time}} (HH:MM) and {{date}} (YYYY-MM-DD) tokens. Missing fields leave the placeholder as-is for debuggability. 8 tests: date token substitution, passthrough for static paths, field replacement, special time/date tokens, missing field preservation, mixed known/unknown fields, realistic journal template.Two public async functions: write_create(transport, module, field_values) -> Result<String> -- partitions fields into frontmatter and body by target/field_type defaults (textarea -> body, all else -> frontmatter), generates frontmatter block, joins body parts, renders the path template, writes via transport.create_file(). Returns the resolved vault path. write_append(transport, module, field_values) -> Result<String> -- renders the module's append_template with field values (or falls back to joining body fields), renders the path template, writes via transport.append_under_heading(). Returns the resolved vault path. Internal partition_fields() helper implements the routing logic: explicit target field config takes precedence, otherwise FieldType::Textarea defaults to body and all other field types default to frontmatter.Both functions bail early with a clear error if called with the wrong write mode.5 tests: full create-mode round-trip (verifies frontmatter content, body separation, and file structure), wrong-mode rejection for both directions, append with rendered template, create with no body fields. FieldTarget in src/config.rs gained Clone derive (required by partition_fields to clone out of an Option<&FieldTarget>) src/lib.rs updated with pub mod output; Test crate root tests/output/main.rs wires frontmatter, template, and orchestration modules YAML quoting of dates: The initial YAML_SPECIAL character set included -, which caused date values like 2025-01-15 to be unnecessarily quoted. Fixed by splitting into YAML_SPECIAL (always-quote characters) and YAML_SPECIAL_START (only-quote-at-start characters like -). Formatting: Several assert macros with long message strings didn't match cargo fmt expectations for line wrapping. Fixed by running cargo fmt before final gate check. FieldTarget Clone: The partition_fields function needed to clone FieldTarget values out of Option references. Added Clone derive to FieldTarget enum -- minimal, safe change to the config module. running 59 tests (13 config + 20 output + 26 transport) config: 13 passed output::frontmatter: 7 passed output::template: 8 passed output::orchestration: 5 passed transport::api: 5 passed transport::fs: 10 passed transport::dispatcher: 6 passed test result: ok. 59 passed; 0 failed Hand-built YAML over serde_yaml: The frontmatter generator builds YAML strings manually rather than using serde_yaml. This avoids a runtime dependency for writing (serde_yaml is still available for reading) and gives precise control over formatting -- Obsidian expects specific YAML conventions that a generic serializer might not produce. Comma-separated detection heuristic: Values containing ", " (comma-space) are treated as lists. This matches the common pattern for tag input in TUI forms. A single comma without a following space is not treated as a list delimiter. Missing placeholders preserved: render_append_template leaves {{unknown}} placeholders in the output rather than replacing them with empty strings. This makes debugging easier -- the user can see which fields were not provided. Partition logic in mod.rs, not config.rs: The field-to-target routing logic lives in the output module rather than on FieldConfig, keeping config.rs focused on parsing/validation and output/mod.rs focused on rendering decisions. The output pipeline is complete and ready to be wired into the TUI: write_create and write_append accept a Transport, a ModuleConfig, and field values -- all of which the TUI will have after form completion The functions return the vault-relative path of the written file, which the TUI can display as confirmation Error handling uses anyhow::Result consistently, ready for TUI error display Next sprint candidates: TUI form screens, dynamic data fetching, or the dashboard view.

item.title: sprint-1-foundation-report
item.description: Sprint 1 established the project foundation: a buildable Rust project with a fully typed, validated configuration layer. All three tasks passed inspection with cargo check, cargo test (13 tests), cargo clippy, and cargo fmt -- --check all clean.Created the project manifest with Rust 2024 edition and all required dependencies: TUI: ratatui, crossterm Serialization: serde (with derive), toml, serde_yaml, serde_json Networking: reqwest (with json + rustls-tls, no OpenSSL dependency on Windows) Async: tokio (with rt-multi-thread, macros, fs) Utilities: chrono, dirs, anyhow Binary name set to pour.Defined all structs and enums for the config layer: Config (top-level: vault + modules HashMap) VaultConfig (base_path, api_port with default 27124, api_key) ModuleConfig (mode, path, append settings, fields, display_name) FieldConfig (name, field_type, prompt, required, default, options, source, target) WriteMode enum: append / create FieldType enum: text, textarea, number, static_select, dynamic_select FieldTarget enum: frontmatter / body All types derive Deserialize + Debug. Enums use #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]. Three unit tests verify round-trip TOML deserialization, default api_port behavior, and minimal config parsing.Implemented Config::load() and Config::from_str() with: File resolution: POUR_CONFIG env var -> ~/.config/pour/config.toml via dirs::config_dir() Typed errors: ConfigError enum with NotFound, ReadError, ParseError, ValidationError variants, plus Display and Error impls Validation rules: Every module must have >= 1 field append mode requires append_under_header static_select requires non-empty options dynamic_select requires source API key resolution: POUR_API_KEY env var takes precedence over config value Ten additional tests covering: valid parse via from_str, each validation failure case, invalid TOML parse error, env var override for API key, file-not-found via env var, and full file loading via POUR_CONFIG. Raw string delimiters (TASK-002): Rust 2024 edition reserves "## sequences. Initial r#"…"# delimiters conflicted with "## Log" in test TOML. Fixed by using r####"…"####. Unsafe env var mutation (TASK-003): Rust 2024 edition made std::env::set_var and remove_var unsafe (not thread-safe). Wrapped all test env var calls in unsafe blocks with safety comments. Clippy collapsible_if (TASK-003): Nested if let + if for API key env var check flagged by clippy. Collapsed into a single if let … && … expression using let-chains (stable in 2024 edition). Formatting (TASK-003): cargo fmt flagged a multi-line let binding that fit on one line. Auto-fixed. running 13 tests test config::tests::load_with_pour_config_env_var_nonexistent_file ... ok test config::tests::invalid_toml_produces_parse_error ... ok test config::tests::module_with_no_fields_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::minimal_config_parses ... ok test config::tests::api_port_defaults_when_omitted ... ok test config::tests::static_select_with_empty_options_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::append_mode_without_header_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::dynamic_select_without_source_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::static_select_without_options_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::round_trip_sample_config ... ok test config::tests::api_key_env_var_overrides_config ... ok test config::tests::valid_config_parses_via_from_str ... ok test config::tests::load_from_pour_config_env_var ... ok test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed Only dead_code warnings for types not yet consumed outside tests. These will resolve as Sprint 2+ code starts using the config types. No clippy lints, no formatting issues.The config layer is solid and ready to be consumed. Sprint 2 (Transport Layer) can begin: TASK-004: API client - can read VaultConfig.api_port and api_key TASK-005: Filesystem writer - can read VaultConfig.base_path and ModuleConfig.path TASK-006: Transport dispatcher - can use Config::load() to get the full config No blockers. The foundation is in place.

item.title: sprint-2-transport-report
item.description: Sprint 2 implemented the hybrid transport layer: an API client for the Obsidian Local REST API, a filesystem writer for direct vault access, and a unified dispatcher that tries the API first and falls back to filesystem. All three tasks passed inspection with cargo check, cargo test (34 tests), cargo clippy, and cargo fmt -- --check all clean.ApiClient struct wrapping reqwest::Client with: Constructor new(port, api_key) building an HTTPS client that accepts self-signed certificates with a 5-second timeout check_connection() -- GET / with Bearer auth, returns bool (catches all errors, never propagates) create_file(vault_path, content) -- PUT to /vault/{path} with Content-Type: text/markdown append_under_heading(vault_path, heading, content) -- PATCH to /vault/{path} using the v3 header-based API (Operation: append, Target-Type: heading, Target: {heading}) list_directory(vault_dir_path) -- GET /vault/{dir}/ (trailing slash), deserializes {"files": […]} JSON response All methods async, returning anyhow::Result with contextual error messages.5 tests: HTTPS scheme validation, port embedding, default port, multi-port sweep, unreachable server returns false.FsWriter struct holding a vault base_path: PathBuf with: create_file(relative_path, content) -- writes file, creates parent directories, errors if file already exists append_to_file(relative_path, content) -- appends to existing file, errors if file not found list_directory(relative_dir_path) -- lists .md files, returns sorted stem names, excludes non-.md files and subdirectories All methods synchronous, returning anyhow::Result with contextual error messages.10 tests: content writing, parent dir creation, duplicate file rejection, append behavior, missing file error, sorted stem listing, subdirectory exclusion, non-directory error, empty directory handling, base_path getter. TransportMode enum (Api / FileSystem) with Display impl for TUI status display Transport enum wrapping ApiClient and FsWriter Transport::connect(config) -- attempts API connection when both api_port and api_key are configured and check_connection() succeeds; falls back to filesystem otherwise Unified create_file, append_under_heading, list_directory methods that delegate to the active backend Filesystem fallback for append_under_heading does a plain append (heading-aware insertion deferred to future sprint) src/lib.rs updated with pub mod transport; 6 tests: no-API-key fallback, unreachable-API fallback, create/append/list delegation through FS backend, TransportMode Display formatting. Clippy collapsible_if (TASK-005): Nested if path.is_file() { if let Some(ext) … { if ext == "md" { … }}} flagged by clippy. Collapsed into a single if with let-chains (Rust 2024 edition). Formatting (TASK-005): Several anyhow::bail! and .with_context() calls had formatting that didn't match cargo fmt expectations. Reformatted. Module wiring: Integration tests in tests/transport/ require the module to be exported from lib.rs. Added minimal pub mod transport; to lib.rs and pub mod api; / pub mod fs; to transport/mod.rs as part of the build-up, rather than deferring all wiring to TASK-006. Test crate structure: tests/transport/ uses main.rs as the crate root (not mod.rs), following Rust's convention for directory-based integration test crates. running 34 tests (13 config + 21 transport) config: 13 passed transport::api: 5 passed transport::fs: 10 passed transport::dispatcher: 6 passed test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed base_url is pub on ApiClient to allow test assertions on URL construction without needing a getter method. list_directory return type differences: The API backend returns raw filenames (e.g., "latte.md", "subdir/"), while the filesystem backend returns .md stems only (e.g., "latte"). This asymmetry is documented; callers will need to normalize. A normalization layer can be added in a future sprint. Filesystem append_under_heading fallback: The FS backend cannot do heading-aware insertion without a markdown parser. It falls back to plain append_to_file. This is documented in the code and acceptable for v1. tempfile crate: Added as a dev-dependency for filesystem tests. Creates OS-managed temporary directories that auto-clean on drop. The transport layer is complete and ready to be consumed. Sprint 3 (Output Rendering) can begin: Output modules can use Transport::create_file and Transport::append_under_heading to write to the vault Data fetching modules can use Transport::list_directory to populate dynamic dropdowns The TUI can display Transport::mode() to show the user which backend is active No blockers. The transport foundation is in place.

item.title: distill-first-pass-spec
item.description:
Distill is a minimal, terminal-native local AI harness for processing Obsidian notes after capture. Where pour is optimized for reflexive entry, distill is optimized for deliberate synthesis. It turns raw notes into reviewable knowledge artifacts without sacrificing source integrity, plaintext portability, or user authority.Core Philosophy: Synthesis After Capture: pour captures first. distill processes later. These responsibilities should stay separate. Source Integrity Above All: The original note is never silently rewritten or discarded. AI Isolation: Machine-generated output must live in explicit sections, sidecar files, or review buffers until accepted. Plaintext Is Still Forever: All durable state is stored as Markdown, YAML, or simple local metadata. No opaque hosted pipeline. Local-First Control: The model, prompts, embeddings, and note context should be operable on-device. distill is not a chatbot wrapped in a TUI. It is a controlled note-processing tool for Obsidian.The application has four primary execution paths:Running the base command opens the main processing queue. Header: Model/provider status, vault readiness, pending review count. Body: Notes ready for processing or review. Sidebar or Tabs: Filters such as inbox, pending, applied, failed. Quick Actions: Start processing, open review, skip, re-run. The queue should feel operational and calm, more like a triage board than a chat session.Bypasses the queue and processes one note directly. snapshots source state runs configured AI passes opens the review surface rather than applying edits automatically This is the equivalent of pour <module>: a direct path for focused work.Opens the pending suggestion workflow.The review view is the core product surface. It should support rapid tabbing through proposal types: summary links entities questions metadata rewrite The left side remains canonical source. The right side shows structured proposals. Acceptance is explicit and granular.The following commands are in scope as first-class routes: distill inbox distill note <path> distill review distill links <path> distill apply These should map to stable internal workflows rather than becoming arbitrary prompt entry points.
distill must inherit guidance from The Pour Manifesto without copying pour's exact interaction model.The manifesto gives four durable constraints: Capture and synthesis are separate acts. pour handles the raw moment. distill handles the slower second pass. Plaintext output matters. AI assistance should not move note processing into a black box or proprietary state store. The tool must get out of the way. distill should reduce note-maintenance friction, not create a sprawling "AI workspace." The command is the ritual. distill should feel like an intentional refinement pass over notes, not a general-purpose assistant shell. The practical implication is: distill must be review-first, bounded, and file-native.Each note should move through a predictable local pipeline: discover candidate note snapshot original state normalize markdown for model input gather vault context run one or more specialized AI passes store proposals in an isolated state representation review proposals in the TUI apply accepted changes back to the note This should be modular. A failed links pass should not invalidate an otherwise successful summary pass.distill should avoid a single giant "improve this note" prompt. The minimum useful passes are: Summary Pass: compress the note into a durable, reviewable synopsis Link Pass: propose [[wikilinks]] to existing vault notes Entity Pass: identify people, places, topics, projects, media, or gear worth linking Metadata Pass: propose tags, aliases, and lightweight structured fields Question Pass: identify unresolved threads or follow-up prompts Optional later pass: Rewrite Pass: propose a cleaner version of the note body without replacing the source by default This is the most important architectural rule.The original note remains canonical until the user applies accepted changes. AI output must be isolated in one of the following ways: explicit note sections such as ## AI Summary or ## Proposed Links sibling sidecar files such as <note>.distill.md local state/cache files outside the vault for intermediate review data Preferred first-pass model: source note remains untouched during processing proposals are written to a sibling .distill.md file or equivalent local state accepted changes are merged back into the note through an explicit apply step This provides: auditability rollback safety clean separation between source and machine output compatibility with Obsidian sync and version control The link pass should consult vault-local context rather than hallucinating note structure.Useful context sources: note titles aliases tags frontmatter metadata nearby folder structure optional embeddings/vector index distill should prefer linking to existing notes over inventing new structure unless explicitly configured to suggest new note creation.The model layer should be provider-agnostic.Examples: local HTTP model server llama.cpp ollama custom local inference bridge The spec should treat model access as a pluggable provider, but all core flows must assume the provider may be slow, imperfect, or occasionally offline.The first-pass TUI should be built around three core screens: Queue: candidate notes, status, and pending work Review: source note vs. AI proposals Apply Summary: accepted operations and resulting file changes The review surface should optimize for fast, repetitive approval work.Required characteristics: source always visible proposals grouped by type tabbing between proposal groups is fast and predictable accept/reject/edit actions are explicit no hidden background mutation of canonical notes Suggested keys: Tab / Shift+Tab to move between proposal panes j / k or arrows to move items a accept r reject e edit A apply all accepted q quit The interface should feel technical, sparse, and trustworthy.Prefer: pending accepted applied source proposal links Avoid: conversational assistant language celebratory AI wording anything that implies the model is authoritative The TUI should read like a careful processing tool, not an AI companion.The source note is the authority.distill may: append accepted summaries insert accepted wikilinks add accepted metadata write derived sidecar files distill must not: silently replace the original body reorder note structure without review delete original content by default The first-pass application layer should support these mutation classes: insert or replace an AI Summary section insert accepted wikilinks into note body or footer block add frontmatter fields such as distill_status, distill_last_run, or tags create a related note stub when explicitly approved Each applied change should be narrow and inspectable.Useful local metadata fields may include: distill_status distill_last_run distill_model distill_reviewed These should remain optional and human-readable.The following are explicitly in scope for v0.1: queue view for candidate notes single-note processing path local provider abstraction for AI execution source snapshotting / persistence isolated proposal storage review UI with proposal tabs link suggestions against existing vault context summary and metadata passes explicit apply step for accepted changes The following are explicitly deferred: autonomous background processing with silent application chat-style prompting inside the main interface aggressive note rewriting as a default workflow multi-user collaboration cloud-only model dependency fully automatic graph restructuring of the vault If pour is the reflex that gets life into the vault, distill is the quiet second pass that makes the vault more legible.distill should help the user: preserve original notes isolate AI output strengthen wiki linking tab through suggestions quickly apply synthesis without surrendering authorship That is the correct complement to the manifesto: capture first, synthesize later, and keep both acts native to plaintext and the terminal.

item.title: implementation-debt-and-dependency-audit
item.description: Validate all module write targets as vault-relative before they reach transport Make config persistence atomic (write-then-rename) Remove serde_yaml Fix README and CLAUDE.md to match actual behavior Stop swallowing browse errors; surface them into status_message Wire real loading/error state into browser or remove BrowserState.loading Add focused tests for configure behavior (input handling, mode toggle, path selection, error UX) Decide configurator scope: narrow scalar-editor vs. full epic from TODO.md Break src/tui/configure.rs into smaller units once behavior stabilizes Reevaluate reqwest if build time or binary size becomes a concern Expand docs under 04 architecture/ if configurator becomes a committed subsystem Review the current implementation and outstanding local changes for technical debt, unnecessary complexity, and external dependency bloat. Prioritize issues that materially affect correctness, maintainability, and release readiness. Current worktree changes on main Core runtime code in src/ New configurator and config-write path Cargo dependency surface from Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, cargo tree, and cargo metadata Existing docs and repo hygiene files that add maintenance overhead The current branch introduces a substantial in-app configurator feature before a few v1 hardening items are closed. The largest risks are: Module write paths are still not validated as vault-relative and safe. The new configure/browse flow blocks the TUI on transport calls and hides browse errors. Config writes are not atomic. serde_yaml appears to be unused dependency bloat. Repo documentation is now out of sync with actual config and transport behavior. The new toml_edit dependency is justified. The new configurator feature is directionally useful, but it expands app, config, transport, and TUI complexity faster than the current test coverage supports.Problemmodule.path is still not rejected when absolute or when it escapes the vault root after normalization. Current validation covers dynamic select source, but not write targets. The filesystem backend joins configured paths directly and can write outside the vault if given a bad path.Why it matters Correctness and safety issue The new configurator makes unsafe edits easier to introduce from inside the app This is already acknowledged in TODO.md as a blocker-level bug Action Extend Config::validate() to reject: absolute paths drive-qualified Windows paths UNC paths normalized traversal outside the vault root Reuse the same validation for: module.path any future multi-path/fallback path feature Add regression tests for both Windows-style and Unix-style path variants Suggested owner files src/config.rs tests/config.rs tests/output/orchestration.rs ProblemEntering the configure screen pre-fetches a directory listing inline from the main event loop. Browsing also performs transport calls inline. API browse failures are turned into empty directory listings via unwrap_or_default(), which misreports errors as "no subdirectories".Why it matters The TUI can freeze for up to the request timeout UX lies to the user on API/filesystem browse failures BrowserState.loading exists but is effectively dead state Action Replace eager configure prefetch with explicit browse open Set browser_state.loading = true before fetch begins Surface errors into status_message instead of converting them to empty results If keeping the current architecture, at minimum distinguish: empty directory failed request invalid path Add focused tests for configure browse state transitions Suggested owner files src/main.rs src/app.rs src/tui/configure.rs src/transport/mod.rs ProblemConfig::update_module_on_disk() validates before writing, but the final write is still a direct overwrite of the live config.toml.Why it matters Partial writes can brick the app until the config is manually repaired This is the highest-risk persistence path because it touches the app's boot-critical file Action Write edited TOML to a sibling temp file rename/replace atomically after validation succeeds Mirror the pattern already used in cache persistence Add a short comment documenting the crash-safety expectation Suggested owner files src/config.rs tests/config_update.rs ProblemThe new configurator touches: app state event dispatch transport listing APIs config persistence a large single-file TUI handler But the only new tests cover config persistence. There is no direct coverage for configure input handling, mode toggling behavior, path selection flow, or error UX.Why it matters High change surface with low confidence Likely source of regressions as the configurator grows Action Add tests for: App::init_configure() mode toggle add/remove of append_under_header configure key handling transitions path browser selection semantics save error message behavior Split pure helper logic from src/tui/configure.rs into testable functions if needed Suggested owner files src/app.rs src/tui/configure.rs tests/app.rs new tests/tui_* or equivalent focused tests ProblemThe README example and assistant guidance no longer match the implementation: README uses type where the code expects field_type README uses vault://… for source, but runtime expects vault-relative paths README implies path interpolation that is not implemented CLAUDE.md describes the API as HTTP while the code uses HTTPS with invalid-cert acceptance Why it matters Misleads future contributors Inflates support/debugging cost Makes feature review harder because the docs are not a trustworthy source of truth Action Update README config examples to match the real schema Correct transport protocol wording Document the current limits of path rendering and dynamic select sources If the configurator is staying, document its current scope honestly Suggested owner files README.md CLAUDE.md optional architecture notes in pour - docs/04 architecture/ Justified. Used pervasively for transport, init, cache, and output orchestration.Justified. Used in path rendering, append templates, frontmatter date injection, and cache timestamps.Justified. Core terminal event/input layer.Justified. Used for config path, cache path, and vault detection.Justified. Core UI dependency.Justified, but it is the heaviest dependency in the tree by a wide margin. Keep it only because hybrid API transport is a first-class product feature.Justified. Central to config and cache parsing.Justified. Required for cache persistence and API response handling.Justified. Required for async main loop and async transport calls.Justified. Required for config parsing.Justified. This is the right tool for comment-preserving TOML mutation. Incremental dependency cost is acceptable because toml already brings it transitively.Justified. Test-only and heavily used across transport/config/output tests.This appears to be unused dependency bloat.Current state Declared in Cargo.toml Not used in runtime code for frontmatter generation Pulls deprecated unsafe-libyaml transitively Action Remove serde_yaml from dependencies Regenerate Cargo.lock Update docs that still imply YAML serialization is crate-backed The extra transport API for typed directory entries is reasonable Using toml_edit for structure-preserving config mutation is a sound tradeoff Dashboard alignment and form title changes are harmless polish src/tui/configure.rs is already carrying rendering, browser state, key handling, mode toggle policy, and path helper logic in one file BrowserState.loading is unused state and should either be wired or removed The current configure feature scope is much smaller than the TODO epic it starts to imply; avoid widening it before hardening what exists The worktree also contains new assistant/tooling artifacts: .claude/ CLAUDE.md If these are not intentional project assets, they should be ignored or excluded before merge to avoid accumulating maintenance surface unrelated to the shipped binary.Current .gitignore only ignores /target. That is not enough if local assistant/editor files are expected to recur. Add vault-relative validation for all module write paths. Make config writes atomic. Remove serde_yaml. Fix README and CLAUDE.md to match actual behavior. Stop swallowing browse errors. Either wire real loading/error state into the browser or remove loading. Add focused tests for configure behavior, not just persistence. Decide whether the configurator remains a narrow scalar-editor or is truly beginning the larger epic described in TODO.md. Break src/tui/configure.rs into smaller units once behavior stabilizes. Reevaluate reqwest only if build time or binary size becomes a product concern. Expand docs under 04 architecture/ if the configurator becomes a committed subsystem. The dependency review was backed by: cargo tree cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps repo-wide symbol usage search cargo test could not be completed in the current Windows environment because Cargo could not write to the target directory due to Access is denied errors. That constraint should be resolved before treating this branch as release-ready.

item.title: pour-design-spec
item.description:
Pour is a blazing-fast, terminal-native (TUI) capture tool designed to eliminate the friction of logging structured data into Obsidian. Built in Rust (using ratatui), it acts as a headless data-entry client, allowing users to rapidly "pour" thoughts and coffee logs directly into their vault without breaking their CLI workflow.Core Philosophy: Offline-First Resilience: Works with the Obsidian Local REST API, but falls back seamlessly to direct file-system operations if the vault is closed. Snappy & Rhythmic: Designed around the pour command. Fast muscle memory. Data Integrity: Generates strict YAML frontmatter and standard Markdown to ensure 100% compatibility with Obsidian Properties (Bases) and Dataview. The application has two primary execution paths:Running the base command opens the main interactive hub. Header: Displays vault connection status (🟢 API Connected | 🟡 Direct File Mode). Body: Shows a summary of today's stats (e.g., "Poured today: 2 Coffees, 1 Journal"). Menu: Navigable list to launch specific modules (me, coffee). Bypasses the dashboard and launches directly into a specific data-entry view. pour me — Opens the journal appending view. pour coffee — Opens the coffee logging form. Upon submitting a form, the app does not immediately exit. It transitions to a Summary View displaying: A success message with the destination file path. Options: [Enter] Main Menu, [A] Pour Another → .., [Q] Quit, [O] Open file in $EDITOR. Pour uses a dual-pronged approach to writing data:
Primary (API): Attempts a fast local HTTP request via reqwest to the Obsidian Local REST API (http://127.0.0.1:27124). Fallback (File System): If the connection is refused, it gracefully falls back to std::fs to write directly to the absolute vault path defined in the configuration. API Authentication: The REST API plugin requires a Bearer token. Pour supports two sources: api_key field under [vault] in config.toml. POUR_API_KEY environment variable (takes precedence over config if set). 3-tier fallback (API → disk scan → cache → freetext) with async background refresh.Append vs. create modes, and how fields map to frontmatter/body.Full TOML schema, field type reference, and validation rules — see config schema section. Language: Rust (2024 Edition)
TUI Framework: ratatui + crossterm
Serialization: serde, serde_json, toml, serde_yaml
Network: reqwest (with tokio for async fetching)
Time: chrono (for file formatting and timestamps) The following are explicitly in scope for v0.1: Dashboard with connection status and module menu pour me (append mode with Templater integration + atomic note fallback) pour coffee (create mode with frontmatter generation) Hybrid transport layer (API → filesystem fallback) Dynamic data fetching (API → disk scan → cache → freetext) Configurable append templates (callout default) Configurable theme (accent color, border style) Post-execution summary view required field validation The following are explicitly deferred: pour music module (generic config supports it when ready) Rich validation (min/max, regex) Tag-based dynamic_select sources Plugin/extension system

This asymmetry is documented; callers will need to normalize. A normalization layer can be added in a future sprint. Filesystem append_under_heading fallback: The FS backend cannot do heading-aware insertion without a markdown parser. It falls back to plain append_to_file. This is documented in the code and acceptable for v1. tempfile crate: Added as a dev-dependency for filesystem tests. Creates OS-managed temporary directories that auto-clean on drop. The transport layer is complete and ready to be consumed. Sprint 3 (Output Rendering) can begin: Output modules can use Transport::create_file and Transport::append_under_heading to write to the vault Data fetching modules can use Transport::list_directory to populate dynamic dropdowns The TUI can display Transport::mode() to show the user which backend is active No blockers. The transport foundation is in place.

item.title: sprint-1-foundation-report
item.description: Sprint 1 established the project foundation: a buildable Rust project with a fully typed, validated configuration layer. All three tasks passed inspection with cargo check, cargo test (13 tests), cargo clippy, and cargo fmt -- --check all clean.Created the project manifest with Rust 2024 edition and all required dependencies: TUI: ratatui, crossterm Serialization: serde (with derive), toml, serde_yaml, serde_json Networking: reqwest (with json + rustls-tls, no OpenSSL dependency on Windows) Async: tokio (with rt-multi-thread, macros, fs) Utilities: chrono, dirs, anyhow Binary name set to pour.Defined all structs and enums for the config layer: Config (top-level: vault + modules HashMap) VaultConfig (base_path, api_port with default 27124, api_key) ModuleConfig (mode, path, append settings, fields, display_name) FieldConfig (name, field_type, prompt, required, default, options, source, target) WriteMode enum: append / create FieldType enum: text, textarea, number, static_select, dynamic_select FieldTarget enum: frontmatter / body All types derive Deserialize + Debug. Enums use #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]. Three unit tests verify round-trip TOML deserialization, default api_port behavior, and minimal config parsing.Implemented Config::load() and Config::from_str() with: File resolution: POUR_CONFIG env var -> ~/.config/pour/config.toml via dirs::config_dir() Typed errors: ConfigError enum with NotFound, ReadError, ParseError, ValidationError variants, plus Display and Error impls Validation rules: Every module must have >= 1 field append mode requires append_under_header static_select requires non-empty options dynamic_select requires source API key resolution: POUR_API_KEY env var takes precedence over config value Ten additional tests covering: valid parse via from_str, each validation failure case, invalid TOML parse error, env var override for API key, file-not-found via env var, and full file loading via POUR_CONFIG. Raw string delimiters (TASK-002): Rust 2024 edition reserves "## sequences. Initial r#"…"# delimiters conflicted with "## Log" in test TOML. Fixed by using r####"…"####. Unsafe env var mutation (TASK-003): Rust 2024 edition made std::env::set_var and remove_var unsafe (not thread-safe). Wrapped all test env var calls in unsafe blocks with safety comments. Clippy collapsible_if (TASK-003): Nested if let + if for API key env var check flagged by clippy. Collapsed into a single if let … && … expression using let-chains (stable in 2024 edition). Formatting (TASK-003): cargo fmt flagged a multi-line let binding that fit on one line. Auto-fixed. running 13 tests test config::tests::load_with_pour_config_env_var_nonexistent_file ... ok test config::tests::invalid_toml_produces_parse_error ... ok test config::tests::module_with_no_fields_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::minimal_config_parses ... ok test config::tests::api_port_defaults_when_omitted ... ok test config::tests::static_select_with_empty_options_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::append_mode_without_header_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::dynamic_select_without_source_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::static_select_without_options_fails_validation ... ok test config::tests::round_trip_sample_config ... ok test config::tests::api_key_env_var_overrides_config ... ok test config::tests::valid_config_parses_via_from_str ... ok test config::tests::load_from_pour_config_env_var ... ok test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed Only dead_code warnings for types not yet consumed outside tests. These will resolve as Sprint 2+ code starts using the config types. No clippy lints, no formatting issues.The config layer is solid and ready to be consumed. Sprint 2 (Transport Layer) can begin: TASK-004: API client - can read VaultConfig.api_port and api_key TASK-005: Filesystem writer - can read VaultConfig.base_path and ModuleConfig.path TASK-006: Transport dispatcher - can use Config::load() to get the full config No blockers. The foundation is in place.
